multi_number_sentence_detail.sentence: On July 13, 2026, U.S. President Donald Trump announced a new plan.

beyond_a2_general.reason: In the sense of making a plan public, this is typically B1 or higher and could be replaced by "say publicly."
This is typically above A2 and could be explained as money that someone must pay.
This shipping-related noun is above typical A2 and could be replaced by the more common word "goods."
Its figurative meaning of abandoning or cancelling a plan is harder than its ordinary physical meaning.
The commercial meaning of buying and selling between countries is typically above A2 and can be explained with simpler words.
The meaning of a commercial agreement is typically B1 and could be replaced by "agreement."
This financial verb is usually above A2 and can be explained as putting money into a country or business.
Its abstract financial meaning of producing or providing money is harder than the ordinary A2 movement sense.
This market-role noun is above A2 and could be explained as a person who buys and sells oil.
Its figurative use meaning to cause a price to rise is above the usual physical A2 sense.
Its financial-market meaning of ending trading at a particular price is above typical A2 and could be replaced by "end."
In "Iran-linked," it means politically or commercially connected, a sense typically above A2.
The abstract phrase "in place," meaning active or operating, is harder than the ordinary A2 location meaning.
The passive use meaning to make someone very surprised is typically B1 and can be expressed with "very surprise."
Its transit-related meaning in "passage fees" is above A2 and could be explained as going through the strait.
This abstract noun is typically above A2 and can be explained as being free or having the right to act.

specialist_exceptions.reason: It identifies the precise geographical type of narrow sea channel central to the story, which "sea" or "route" alone would not fully express.
It specifies unrefined oil and forms part of the exact commodity name Brent crude oil, so removing it would reduce market precision.
It is the standard unit used for the quoted oil prices, and replacing it would change or obscure the measurement.
It describes a formal, organized restriction on ship movement that is central to the continuing risk in the story.
It specifies that the attacks were carried out by armed forces, a distinction that simpler words such as "fighting" would lose.
It is part of the formal vessel class "Very Large Crude Carrier," whose standardized type is relevant to the proposed fee.
It identifies a ship specifically designed to carry oil or other liquids, which the simpler word "ship" would not convey.
It refers to the commercial sea-transport industry, not merely to ships themselves, and that industry context matters here.
It names the exact kind of charge imposed for passing through a route and is central to the disputed plan and legal rule.
It is essential to the established legal concept "freedom of navigation," which concerns lawful ship movement through international waters.

uncertain.reason: Its familiarity depends strongly on learners' geographical and cultural context, so its general CEFR level is unclear.
The word itself is elementary, but its abstract use meaning that a plan is feasible or successful may fall around the A2–B1 boundary.

vocab_qa.method_note: This classification is a semantic judgment call based on typical A2 ability, not a lookup against a validated or authoritative CEFR-A2 wordlist; inflected forms were lemmatized, names were treated as named units, and genuinely borderline contextual senses were placed under uncertain.
